newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures hold gains late on cash, cold.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures hold gains late on cash, cold.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held gains late Monday in sluggish trade, with reports of firmer cash prices and forecasts for cold weather this week lifting the complex, industry sources said.
At 1415 EST, December was still up by 5.6 cents at $2.725 per million British thermal units, while January was six cents higher at $2.735. Others were up by 1.6 to 6.7 cents.

"It's looking more constructive. Last week, we held some nice long-term trendlines, but we need to get through $2.745 (basis December)," said one New York-based futures trader, adding cold weather this week should push prices higher.

But traders said bullish sentiment from the cold this week was somewhat muted by forecasts for more seasonal weather next week, leading some to expect only limited gains from the season's first real cold snap.

Technically, most agreed a December close above resistance at $2.745 should lead to a move into the $2.80s and possibly a test of the $2.88 contract high. Key support was still pegged in the $2.52-2.53 area.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Monday to the low-$2.70s. Midwest prices also were modestly higher in the low-$2.60s. Cold Northeast weather this week drove New York city gate gas prices up another dime or more to the high-$3.20s.
NYMEX said 16,395 contracts traded at 1345 EST.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas was still up by one-half cent at a new contract high of $1.295. Other months remained untraded at 1415 EST. NYMEX said one Alberta lot changed hands as of 1345 EST.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded at 1415 EST.
On the KCBT, December gained five cents to $2.535, while January was still 6.5 cents higher at $2.53. The December East/West spread widened by 0.6 cent to 19.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
